title: Exact replay of M1 after a completed session
plain_english: The attacker recorded M1 of a successful login and sends the identical bytes again.
attacker: Passive capture + retransmission on the open channel.
action: Resend M1 unchanged to the 6LC (clock unchanged, inside DeltaT).
steps: 1st delivery: ACCEPT
2nd delivery: REJECT (alias lookup in the 6LC database)
6LC replay-cache sets contain 0 entries (present in the class, never filled by step_ake2)
observed: Step AKE2: AID6LN not found in 6LC database
interpretation: Rejection comes from the STATE TRANSITION after the first session (the stored Sc and alias are replaced), not from a replay cache or the timestamp (still fresh). This is a property of the reconstructed state update, not a literal paper mechanism.

title: Replay of M1 before the sensor has processed M2
plain_english: The same M1 reaches the controller twice in a row (duplicate delivery).

2nd: REJECT (alias lookup in the 6LC database)
observed: Step AKE2: AID6LN not found in 6LC database
interpretation: The controller updates state immediately after the first AKE2, so the duplicate fails.

title: Replay of M1 from the SECOND completed session
plain_english: Replay an M1 recorded in a later session (after the stored state has already been rotated once).
action: Run 3 sessions; resend session 2's M1 (timestamp still fresh).
steps: replay: REJECT (alias lookup in the 6LC database)
observed: Step AKE2: AID6LN not found in 6LC database
interpretation: Rejected: the reconstructed alias rotation changes the stored state every session, so a recorded M1 is only valid once.

title: Future-dated timestamp (+3600 s)
plain_english: A message stamped one hour in the future.
attacker: Controls a clock or edits the unauthenticated timestamp.
action: Deliver an M1 whose T6LN is 3600 s ahead of the controller's clock.
steps: response: ACCEPT
observed: accepted
interpretation: The code tests `tr - T6LN > DeltaT` only, so negative differences always pass. Minor, but a real deviation from the paper's |Tr - T| form.

title: Timestamp refresh on an intercepted, undelivered M1 (delay attack)
plain_english: The attacker blocks M1, waits until it is stale, rewrites only the timestamp to 'now' and delivers it.
attacker: Active man-in-the-middle on the channel; no secrets needed.
action: Replace T6LN by the current time (all other fields untouched), deliver to the 6LC, withhold M2.
steps: forged M1: ACCEPT
attacker withholds M2 (sensor never sees it)
sensor's next honest M1: REJECT (alias lookup in the 6LC database)
observed: accepted
interpretation: T6LN is not covered by the tag, so the old M1 passes. The controller then updates its state while the sensor does not: the two sides are desynchronised and later honest sessions fail (DoS). The attacker cannot learn SK.

title: Timestamp refresh on an already-completed M1

interpretation: Protection again comes from the state update (stored Sc/alias changed), not from timestamp integrity.

title: M1 ciphertext modified
plain_english: One bit of M1's CT is flipped in transit.
action: Flip one bit of CT.
steps: response: REJECT (tag verification of M1)
no plaintext is used after the failed tag comparison (state unchanged)
observed: Step AKE2: Tag6LN mismatch (message integrity/authenticity check failed)
interpretation: Tag = HMAC-SHA256(Kc, AD||CT)[:128 bit] compared in constant time. The inverse-free cipher still computes a plaintext, but it is discarded before any use.

interpretation: There is no recovery path: the controller keeps no previous state and the sensor cannot resynchronise. A single lost M2 permanently locks the device out until re-registration.

title: Denial-of-service considerations (local processing cost only)
plain_english: How much work does the controller do before rejecting garbage? No network flooding is performed.
attacker: Message flooder (simulated locally, 200 calls per case).
action: Feed malformed / forged M1 to step_ake2 in a local loop and count operations.
steps: wrong-length fields (truncated CT): REJECT via 'unhandled ValueError (no explicit validation)'; logical ops/msg {'xor': 4.0, 'hash': 2.0}; ~85.1 us/msg (local, 200 msgs)
random alias (unknown D): REJECT via 'alias lookup in the 6LC database'; logical ops/msg {'xor': 1.0}; ~33.6 us/msg (local, 200 msgs)
valid alias + forged tag (D captured in flight): REJECT via 'tag verification of M1'; logical ops/msg {'xor': 4.0, 'hash': 2.0, 'aead-decrypt': 1.0, 'compare': 1.0}; ~135.6 us/msg (local, 200 msgs)
observed: rejected; costs shown
interpretation: Unknown aliases are rejected after one XOR and a dictionary lookup; a known alias with a forged tag forces key derivation and an AEAD decryption per message; malformed lengths are rejected by unhandled ValueError (works, but not graceful). The code has no rate limiting.

rows: valid alias + forged tag (D captured in flight)

title: Passive keystream-reuse analysis of one session (M1 xor M2)
plain_english: An eavesdropper XORs the two ciphertexts of one session.
attacker: Passive eavesdropper; sees only M1 and M2.
action: CT xor CT1 = (A||B) xor (Sc1||RN2); second half = B xor RN2 = AID6LN xor RN1 xor RN2; RN1, RN2 are public, so AID6LN falls out; TID6LC = D xor AID6LN.
steps: recovered AID6LN equals the true AID6LN: True
recovered TID6LC equals the true TID6LC: True
observed: AID6LN and TID6LC recovered
interpretation: M1 and M2 are encrypted with the SAME Si (the paper itself says Si' is used for CT1; the audited code uses Si'' = Si'), i.e. same AES-CTR key and counter block, hence the same keystream. Reported as a weakness of the specified construction, not of the stand-in cipher: any nonce-based AEAD fails under key+nonce reuse.

title: Passive attempt to compute SK from the transcript (with AID6LN recovered via A17)

steps: session key among 100 guesses: False
observed: not derived in this attempt
interpretation: SK still needs B1 (RN2 xor K6LN) and Sc1, both secret; the tested guesses failed. This is NOT a proof of secrecy.
